title: Short Adjectives Practice
description: Extra practice with short adjective forms
intro: Practice choosing the correct short adjective form and knowing when to use short vs long forms. Short adjectives only appear as predicates (after the subject): Он болен. They agree in gender and number but NOT case. Some adjectives exist only in short form: рад, готов, должен, нужен. Others have both forms: красивый/красив, больной/болен. When both exist, the short form often suggests a temporary state, while the long form describes a permanent quality.
rules: Short adjectives are ONLY used as predicates (after the subject): Дом красив. NEVER before a noun — use long form: красивый дом.
Long form before a noun (attributive): новая книга. Long or short after the subject (predicate): Книга новая. / Книга нова.
Short forms agree in gender and number: masculine -∅ (готов), feminine -а (готова), neuter -о (готово), plural -ы/-и (готовы).
Common short-only adjectives: рад (glad), готов (ready), должен (must), нужен (needed), согласен (agree), доволен (satisfied). These have no long-form equivalent in the same meaning.
examples: Я рада вас видеть. (I'm glad to see you.), feminine speaker, short only
Он должен работать. (He must work.), masculine, short only
Дом красив. (The house is beautiful.), short form, temporary impression
Красивый дом стоит на горе. (A beautiful house stands on the hill.), long form before noun

items.prompt: Она _____ помочь вам. (She is ready to help you.)
items.promptEnglish: She is ready to help you.
items.explanation: Short adjective: готова (feminine). Готов is short-only in this meaning.

items.prompt: Мы _____ новостям. (We are glad about the news.)
items.promptEnglish: We are glad about the news.
items.explanation: Short adjective: рады (plural). Рад is short-only.

items.prompt: Мне _____ ваша помощь. (I need your help.)
items.explanation: Нужна agrees with помощь (feminine). Short-only adjective.

items.prompt: Он _____ с вами. (He agrees with you.)
items.hint: Masculine short form with fleeting vowel
items.explanation: Short adjective: согласен (masculine, fleeting е). Short-only in this meaning.
Short adjective: легка (feminine). As a predicate, short form is preferred.
Short adjective: должны (plural). Должен is short-only.

items.prompt: Мне _____ это сделать. (I need to do this.)
items.explanation: Нужно + infinitive is an impersonal construction (neuter).
Short adjective: красива (feminine). As predicate, short form works.

items.prompt: Я _____ результатом. (I am satisfied with the result.) - masculine speaker
items.promptEnglish: I am satisfied with the result.
items.hint: Masculine short form with fleeting vowel
items.explanation: Short adjective: доволен (masculine, fleeting е). Short-only in this meaning.

blanks: Он _____ результатом. (He is satisfied with the result.)
Она _____ помочь вам. (She is ready to help you.)
Он _____ с вами. (He agrees with you.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Short adjective gender agreement: masculine vs feminine forms
hints: Он is masculine. Больной has a fleeting vowel in the masculine short form. What is it?
Она is feminine. What is the feminine short form of больной?
Он is masculine. What is the masculine short form of довольный? (Fleeting vowel.)
Она is feminine. What is the feminine short form of готовый?
Он is masculine. What is the masculine short form of согласный? (Fleeting vowel.)
explanations: Masculine short form: больной → болен (fleeting е). Он болен сегодня.
Feminine short form: больной → больна. Она больна сегодня.
Masculine short form: довольный → доволен (fleeting е). Он доволен результатом.
Feminine short form: готовый → готова. Она готова помочь вам.
Masculine short form: согласный → согласен (fleeting е). Он согласен с вами.

minimalPairs.context: _____ дом стоит на горе. (A beautiful house stands on the hill.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: A beautiful house stands on the hill.
minimalPairs.explanation: Before a noun (attributive position), ALWAYS use the long form: красивый дом.
As a predicate (after the subject), the short form is natural: Дом красив. (The long form красивый is also possible here, but short is preferred for this pattern.)

categorySorting.instruction: Sort: Short form only or Both forms exist?
